questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a great opportunity to meet students from other countries. It was also a very important subject and fits into my education. It is a nice city and the crew in the hostel was very nice. That the course was paid for was also crucial since students often live on a budget.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teachers were very dedicated. It is clear that things work differently in the three countries and that there are multiple study methods.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. There were many confusing emails, and we should have had much more time for the online learning agreement for example. The information was unclear and it would have been nice to feel more prepared with more than one meeting before coming to Italy. The meeting was also cancelled at first and then rearreged very late. Overall it would have been nice with some more clear information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The teachers were not here upon arrival and therefore we were a little confused about what to do since we were asked to be here at 17:00. This had no purpose since it was self-check-in at the hostel, and we didn't get information about the program but only about the hostel.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The accomdations was arrenged for us.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The kitchen rules were not explained to us even though we had to do the dishes and prepare breakfast. Also, it could be nice to be able to eat something else than cake for breakfast and maybe also some salad for lunch and dinner :) We also ate too much pizza with fries on it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were too many steps and pages for doing this. It would also have been nice to know more about the deadlines and to have all information in English (not Italian).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine writing the application but way to hard to find information afterwords. I think that we should also have been handed the money before going like some of the other students did as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not relevant

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It would have been nice if the teachers knew more about the possibility to write an essay afterward or how to get etcs points from the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very fun course but we got split up a lot. Therefore the was sometimes a feeling of missing something important because we were divided into groups. It felt like there was some academical differences and different levels as well. But overall it was very fun to meet students from other countries and to understand the way off their living and studentlife.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As a geography student, a lot of the subjects were something that we have worked with before. Therefore the academic level didn't feel that high, but at the same time, it was very interesting to hear totally different opinions and ideas on different subjects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different, but not that far from what we are used to. The differences between the three countries were huge. There is a feeling of Italians students not being used to reading and that all students are not used to making presentations in front of the class.
